newsitem.title: Philippines: Manila call loan rate unchanged in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rate unchanged in liquid market.

text.p: With the Central Bank keeping a floor on interest rates at 10.5 percent, Philippine interbank call loan rates were unchanged at an average of 10.53125 percent in a very liquid market, traders said on Wednesday.
The Central Bank has been maintaining an overnight borrowing rate of 10.50 percent.
Done rates ranged from 10.5625 to 10.53125 percent, with volume thinning to 3.683 billion from 4.930 pesos.
"The market is still liquid," a trader said, although banks had been drained of 11 billion pesos in tax remittances and another 5.0 billion pesos for T-bonds to be paid later in the week.
Liquidity in the market has increased after banks were discouraged from investing back their money in reverse repos due to a 20 percent tax.
At the secondary market of T-bills, banks were buying 91-day T-bills to meet clients' requirements.
They have also been trying to sell their longer-term bills with maturities of six months and higher.
Banks plan to buy back these bills later when interest rates are at more attractive levels, dealers said.
A Reuter poll of six institutions showed banks with bid rates of 10.65 to 10.70 percent for three-month bills.
Offer rates for six-month bills were from 10.95 to 11.125 percent; and for one year, 11.40 to 11.50 percent.
